recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source change is needed for FHIR-24681 unless Patient Care reopens the later AdverseEvent timing model.
issue_request: FHIR-24681 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and requested renaming AdverseEvent.date to occurrence, with dateTime, Period, and Timing choices, to align with Event.occurrence[x].
initial_application: Jira comments identify PR #694 commits af7e02d and f430558. Commit af7e02d changed the then-current AdverseEvent spreadsheet from AdverseEvent.date dateTime to AdverseEvent.occurrence[x] dateTime | Period | Timing and tagged it GF#24681; f430558 updated the related search parameter description.
additional_context: Later Applied FHIR-37718 removed the generic top-level AdverseEvent.occurrence[x] as ambiguous and replaced it with more specific timing elements, cause[x] and effect[x], without Timing. Later Applied FHIR-47827 moved cause[x] to AdverseEvent.suspectEntity.occurrence[x]. Current fhir.ini keeps AdverseEvent active and maps both legacy AdverseEvent.date and AdverseEvent.occurrence[x] to current AdverseEvent.effect[x].
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source no longer has AdverseEvent.date, defines AdverseEvent.effect[x] with dateTime and Period, includes an effect search parameter, and uses occurrence only for suspectEntity.occurrence after FHIR-47827. Reintroducing top-level occurrence[x] or Timing would conflict with later applied decisions.
